reviews.one_line_contribution: Admit items into an agent memory bank on their measured leave-one-out contribution inside the top-k bundle they are actually retrieved into (rather than on episode success or reflector confidence), and then audit whether the screen's own projected gain survives its estimation noise by splitting the projected-minus-realized gap into a winner's-curse term and an item-item interference term.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two lines threaten it, and the proposal engages only the first. (i) Data-valuation-for-ICL: Nguyen & Wong (2023) influence-based example selection, plus the Data Shapley / Banzhaf-for-demonstrations line, which exists precisely because leave-one-out valuation is known to be wrong under interaction among selected examples. The proposal's 'non-additivity' finding is the standard motivation for Shapley-style estimators, so E3b's singleton-vs-LOO result would rediscover a known property of LOO valuation rather than establish a new one, and the paper never explains why LOO was chosen over the estimator the field already uses for this exact failure. (ii) Selection-on-noise in model/hyperparameter selection: Cawley & Talbot (JMLR 2010) on over-fitting in model selection and subsequent selection bias in performance evaluation is the same in-sample/unbiased/realized decomposition the paper calls its hardest-to-duplicate contribution; transplanting it to memory items with EB shrinkage is a competent application, not a new statistical result. What is genuinely unclaimed is the retrieval-neighborhood conditioning of the estimand for agentic memory; that is a real but narrow delta, and it is the piece the proposal has deliberately de-emphasized in favor of the decomposition.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline decomposition in E3/P4 is not identified, so the paper's load-bearing claim cannot be adjudicated by the experiment as designed. Two breaks. First, retained-set mismatch: G_insample and G_unbiased are defined over 'the same retained set' from split-half probes (m approx 5.8/item), while G_actual comes from an end-to-end bank whose EB/FDR screen is fit on the full probe data (m approx 11.7). Those are different banks, so G_unbiased - G_actual mixes a genuine transfer gap with a change in the selection rule's sample size, and the 'costs zero extra episodes' oracle projection is an oracle for a bank nobody deploys. Second, and worse, bundle refill: after screening, the agent re-retrieves top-7 from the *screened* bank, so items ranked 8, 9, 10 in the original bank get promoted into bundles whose utility was never probed, and every retained item's utility was measured conditional on the presence of the very items screening removed. G_unbiased = sum of retained u_hat is therefore not an unbiased projection of realized gain even with infinite probes and perfect additivity. The residual G_unbiased - G_actual is a garbage-can term (interference + refill/promotion + neighborhood redefinition because the neighborhood is defined by the bank + train/test query shift + k shrinking below 7 in sparse neighborhoods, which reintroduces the volume lever the pilot already showed is causal). P4's refutation branch -- 'the non-additivity component dominates ... interference is implicated ... screen bundles, not items' -- is thus an unsupported attribution, and the abstract's claim that 'the mechanism is identified rather than asserted' is false as written. Two supporting problems make this worse. (a) Discreteness and coverage: 400 probe queries x 7 slots = 2,800 observations spread over 240 items under a skewed dense-retrieval distribution, so 11.7/item is a mean over a power law; a substantial tail of items will be retrieved zero or one time and have no estimable utility at all, and the proposal states no policy for what happens to never-retrieved items (retain? drop? they are also never injected at eval, which silently makes the screen partly a no-op). At split-half this is m = 0-2 for the tail, and E4's 'effective m in {2,4,7,12}' pretends m is uniform. Each observation is y_full - y_minus_m in {-1,0,+1} on EM with a 7B ReAct agent, where most probes will be concordant zeros, so most items' u_hat is exactly 0 and the ratio-of-noisy-sums quantities in P4 (>=40%, <25%, <15% of 'the naive rule's projected gain') have a denominator that can be near zero and CIs that will not exclude anything at n=240. (b) P2's 25% sign-flip threshold has no noise-matched null: two independent estimates of the *same* utility at m approx 6 would flip sign at a high rate purely from sampling, so as stated P2 cannot distinguish 'utility is neighborhood-conditional' from 'utility is unmeasurable at this budget' -- and the proposal already has the right comparator (within-neighborhood split-half A vs B) but does not use it.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Make the three G quantities share one object: fit the deployed screen on split A only, deploy exactly that bank end-to-end, and reserve split B purely as the unbiased re-estimate; report the full-data screen separately. 2) Break the residual apart instead of naming it. Add a frozen-bundle cell in which the screened items are removed from the already-probed top-7 bundles with no refill (k drops), alongside the re-retrieved screened cell; the difference isolates promotion/refill, and only what remains can be called interference. Without that cell, drop the interference language from P4 and report the residual as unattributed. 3) Give P2 a noise-matched null: compare global-vs-neighborhood sign disagreement against neighborhood-split-half sign disagreement at the identical m, and claim conditionality only on the excess. 4) Report the per-item retrieval-coverage distribution up front, pre-register the treatment of items with zero or one probe, and restate every m as a distribution rather than a mean. 5) Run the ceiling before the grid: an oracle item-level screen fit directly on the held-out set. If the oracle cannot produce +3.5 points, no realizable item-level screen can, and the 12-cell end-to-end grid should not be run -- this is a far more decisive gate than Risk 2's 'P(u>0)>0.7 for >=15% of items'. 6) Reallocate budget. The pilot's own effects were 6-7 items broken, i.e. roughly 1-2 points, yet the pre-registered claim threshold is 3.5 points; as written, 12,000 episodes are spent on twelve contrasts that are pre-declared unclaimable at the effect size the pilot actually observed. Four cells at n=3,000 would decide something; twelve at n=1,000 will not.
reviews.missing_baseline: A bundle-level selection baseline at matched probe budget -- greedy forward/backward subset selection over the bank, or a Shapley/Banzhaf-style estimator, using the same 3,200 probe episodes. This is the direct competitor implied by the proposal's own interference hypothesis, and its absence is structural: if P4's refutation branch fires and non-additivity dominates, the recommended remedy ('screen bundles, not items') has no arm in the design and the paper ends with a diagnosis and no method. All twelve end-to-end cells are item-level screens or content-blind heuristics. Secondarily missing: the oracle screen fit on the held-out set as an upper bound on what any item-level screen can deliver in this setup.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is a non-check and must be scored as such. It reports two consecutive rounds in which every query failed with a tool error, zero titles retrieved, zero dates confirmed, and an explicitly unverified recollection list. The proposal is right to refuse to fabricate a table and right that silence is a tooling failure rather than evidence -- but under any reasonable standard novelty here is unestablished, which is a weakness and not a neutral. Named candidates the authors themselves flag and cannot date: Memory-R1-style RL memory managers (an arXiv preprint of roughly Aug 2025) and ReasoningBank-style experience distillation (roughly Sept 2025); I cannot verify those dates either and neither can the submission. The more likely collision is not in the agent-memory line at all but in demonstration/data valuation, where per-example counterfactual utility with shrinkage or influence approximations for retrieval-augmented ICL is an active 2025 area; a preprint doing per-example counterfactual valuation conditioned on the retrieved context would take the estimand contribution outright. The pre-emptive retargeting to the winner's-curse decomposition is a sensible hedge in principle, but it hedges onto the very analysis whose identification I object to above, so the fallback is weaker than the authors believe. At minimum the search must be executed before this is submittable, and the committed manual protocol (arXiv cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.LG sweeps from 2024-09, forward citations of ExpeL/MIPROv2/ReasoningBank/Memory-R1) should add data-valuation queries: 'Shapley in-context demonstration selection', 'context-conditional data valuation retrieval', 'selection bias example valuation LLM'.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement study that replaces write-time credit signals for agent-memory admission with per-item leave-one-out utility estimated inside the deployed top-k bundle and averaged over the item's retrieval neighborhood, and then asks whether that screen survives its own estimation noise by splitting projected-minus-realized gain into a winner's-curse term and an item-interference term.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two lines, and the proposal under-argues against both. (1) Leave-one-out / influence / Shapley valuation of in-context examples: Nguyen and Wong 2023 is cited, but the broader data-valuation line (Data Shapley and LOO-influence data selection) already establishes per-example marginal utility estimated by ablation, plus the standard finding that such estimates are dominated by variance at small sample sizes. The proposal's differentiator is that utility is conditioned on the retrieval neighborhood and measured inside the deployed bundle, which reads as a deployment-distribution implementation detail of the same estimator rather than a new estimand; the mixed-effects item x neighborhood decomposition (E2/P2) is the only place it becomes a distinct claim, and P2's item-level threshold (25 percent sign flips, 30 percent of explained variance) is not calibrated against what pure sampling noise would produce at m ~ 6 binary paired observations per split, where sign flips near 50 percent are the null expectation. (2) Memory curation from downstream signal: Memory-R1-style RL memory managers, ReasoningBank, Agent Workflow Memory, Mem0/A-MEM/Memento. The proposal names these and matches compute on one of them, which is the right move. Separately, the statistical apparatus is textbook: winner's curse and shrinkage corrections for selection on noisy estimates are standard in model/hyperparameter selection (Cawley and Talbot on selection overfitting) and in bias correction for adaptively collected data (best-arm identification bias). So the contribution is the application target, not the machinery, and that is a 5-level novelty at best.
reviews.strongest_objection: The load-bearing decomposition in E3/P4 is not identified as written. G_unbiased is defined as the sum over retained items of the split-half utility u_i^(B), and these u_i are, by the proposal's own central argument, quantities defined only relative to the specific bundle B(q) they were measured in. But the EB-screened cell (cell 4) is evaluated at k=7 over a SMALLER bank, so for every probe query the deleted items are replaced by items that were originally ranked 8, 9, 10... and were therefore never in any probed bundle and never had their utility estimated at all. Screening here is not deletion, it is substitution with unmeasured items. Consequently G_unbiased - G_actual is a garbage-can residual that mixes (i) genuine item-item interference, (ii) the utility of promoted, never-probed items, (iii) probe-to-heldout retrieval shift, and (iv) the failure of additivity of LOO effects even among retained items. P4's refutation branch ("non-additivity dominates and is stable in m, therefore interference is the mechanism") cannot be reached from this design, because (ii) and (iii) do not shrink in m either. The second, compounding objection is estimator degeneracy: the outcome is string-matched EM, so each of the ~11.7 observations per item is a paired binary difference in {-1,0,+1}, and at pilot-level discordance rates the expected number of NON-ZERO observations per item per split half is well under one. The majority of items will have u_i^(A) exactly 0, the naive rule "keep if u_i > 0" will be decided by one or two lucky flips, and split-half correlation will be near zero. In that regime G_insample - G_unbiased is close to 100 percent of the projected gain by construction, so P4's headline prediction (>=40 percent winner's curse) is confirmed whether or not any utility signal exists, and the design cannot separate "utility exists but is noisily measured" from "utility is not measurable at this budget, so the entire admission criterion is vacuous." A pre-registered prediction that is true under its own null is not a test.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four concrete changes, in priority order. (1) Fix the projection so it applies to the bundle that is actually injected: either hold bundle composition constant under screening (drop an item and leave the slot empty or filled with a neutral placeholder, so no rank-8+ unprobed item is promoted), or re-probe the retained bank's post-screen bundles and define G_unbiased on those. Without this, the non-additivity residual is uninterpretable and P4 should not be the headline. (2) Report, before running, the expected number of discordant (non-zero) LOO observations per item at the pilot's flip rate, and if it is below roughly 2 per split half, switch the utility outcome to a continuous score (F1, or token-level/logprob margin on the gold answer) or raise m; the current design spends 3,200 episodes to produce mostly exact zeros. (3) Add an oracle-screen ceiling cell: fit the keep/drop rule directly on the held-out set (deliberately cheating) and evaluate end-to-end. If the oracle ceiling is below the pre-registered 3.5-point claim threshold, the entire 12-cell end-to-end grid is known in advance to be undecidable and the budget should be reallocated to the item-level analyses; this cell costs 1,000 episodes and is the single highest-information run in the plan. (4) Execute the literature search. The proposal's own admission that no search was performed means novelty is unestablished at submission time, and the pre-emptive retargeting argument is a hedge, not a clearance. Separately: E5 is contingent on P3 clearing 3.5 points (if EB-vs-no-memory lands at +2 under instruction A, "the advantage survives under B" has no advantage to survive), which is the same unestimable-contrast defect the proposal used to justify cutting the GEPA arm; either restructure E5 as an item-level rank-correlation-only analysis or cut it. Also, a 95th percentile cannot be estimated from 3 null replicates, so the stated noise-floor rule needs a parametric or permutation formulation.
reviews.missing_baseline: A randomized-bundle regression (or Shapley-style) attribution estimator at matched EPISODE budget. The LOO design burns 8 runs per probe query to get 7 observations; a design that samples one random 7-item bundle per query and runs it once buys 3,200 distinct queries instead of 400, then regresses the episode outcome on the bundle membership indicator matrix to recover per-item marginal utilities. This is the standard way to de-confound shared episode-level credit, it is far stronger than the Thompson-sampling curator the proposal uses as its RL straw competitor (baseline 8, which credits reward to all 7 co-injected items and will obviously lose), and at equal cost it may well have LOWER per-item variance than paired LOO despite being unpaired. Since the paper's premise is that paired counterfactual estimation is the right estimator and that the winner's curse is large at realistic budgets, an estimator that trades pairing for 8x more queries is exactly the comparison that decides the premise, and it is absent. Ablation (d), which recomputes unpaired differences on the SAME LOO runs, does not substitute for it because it holds the query count fixed. A secondary omission: no oracle/cheating screen to establish the achievable ceiling.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is not thin, it is empty, and the proposal says so: two consecutive rounds of tooling failure, zero queries executed, zero titles or dates retrieved, and an explicit statement that the proposal has not been cleared against the last twelve months of arXiv. The honesty is creditable and the refusal to fabricate a CLOSEST/GAP table is the right call, but per the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a direct hit on the novelty score and on the verdict. I cannot verify dates either, but the risk surface the proposal itself lists is exactly where a 2025-2026 preprint is most likely to sit: utility-based or reward-based memory pruning in the Memory-R1 / ReasoningBank / Mem0 / A-MEM / Memento cluster, and LOO/influence/Shapley valuation of in-context demonstrations. The proposal's fallback argument -- that a colliding preprint would leave the winner's-curse decomposition intact as a qualifying methods contribution -- only holds if that decomposition is sound, and per my strongest objection it currently is not, so the collision hedge is load-bearing on a component that itself needs repair. Given that the committed pre-submission search protocol is described but not executed, novelty here is asserted, not established, and a reviewer is entitled to treat it as unresolved.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A retrieval-neighborhood-conditional leave-one-out estimator of a memory item's marginal utility inside the bundle it is actually injected in, plus a split-half accounting intended to split the gap between a screen's projected and realized gain into a winner's-curse component and an item-interference component.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two lines, neither of which the proposal disposes of. (1) Per-example counterfactual valuation for in-context learning: influence-based selection (the cited Nguyen & Wong 2023) and the Shapley/LOO demonstration-valuation line more broadly already compute exactly y_full - y_{-m} style quantities per example and already screen on them. The proposal's increment is conditioning the average on the retrieval neighborhood rather than a global validation sample - a real but narrow increment, and one that survives only if P2 is actually established, which as designed it cannot be (see strongest_objection). (2) The statistical half is transplantation, not invention: winner's curse, Tweedie/EB shrinkage, and BH-FDR applied to selection on noisy per-unit estimates are textbook, and the closely analogous finding that prompt-optimizer / demonstration-set selection overfits its own validation scores is already circulating for MIPRO/GEPA-class optimizers. If that result exists in the 2025-26 preprint literature for prompt optimization (which the authors did not check), 'the same thing, one slot over, for memory items' is an incremental application. The RL memory-curation line (Memory-R1-style) is correctly identified as the dangerous neighbour but is then instantiated as a strawman (see missing_baseline).
reviews.strongest_objection: P4 is declared the load-bearing prediction and it is not identified. The screened bank is a *smaller bank*, so top-7 retrieval on held-out queries backfills items that ranked 8, 9, 10... in the unscreened bank. Those promoted items appear in deployed bundles whose composition was never probed, and their utility was estimated (if at all) in a different bundle. That effect lands entirely in the residual G_unbiased - G_actual, which P4 and its refutation clause read as 'non-additivity / interference among co-injected items'. Worse, the E4 discriminator fails: backfill does not shrink with probe budget m either, so the proposal's stated test ('winner's curse shrinks in m, non-additivity does not') cannot separate interference from re-retrieval composition change or from probe/test neighborhood shift. The paper would then report 'interference' for an artifact of deleting items from a ranked index. Second, and possibly fatal earlier in the pipeline: the per-item SNR. Utility observations are paired binary EM deltas in {-1,0,+1}; with a discordance rate of the 10-20% the proposal itself assumes and m = 12, SE(u_hat_i) is roughly sqrt(0.15/12) = 0.11, i.e. about 11 accuracy points, while any plausible true per-item marginal effect is a fraction of a point. u_hat_i is then essentially pure noise, and P1's requirement that split-half measured utility reach AUC >= 0.65 - the one signal that must beat the write-path signals for the paper to have a screen at all - is the bet the whole design rests on, and the arithmetic says it lands near 0.5. Third, P2's thresholds are calibrated below the noise-only null in the wrong direction: two independent noisy estimates of near-zero quantities disagree in sign roughly 40-50% of the time, so '>= 25% of items flip sign between global and neighborhood estimates' is confirmed by measurement noise with no neighborhood conditionality present at all; the same objection voids E3b's singleton-vs-LOO sign-flip rate and P6's rank-correlation >= 0.4. Relatedly, the mixed-effects claim that '>= 30% of explained variance' is item x neighborhood interaction is not estimable: with exactly one observation per (item, query) cell, the interaction variance component is aliased with the Bernoulli residual and is set by whatever the model assumes, not by the data.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: All the essential fixes are analysis-level and cost zero extra episodes, which is why this is borderline rather than reject. (1) Calibrate every sign-flip, correlation, and AUC statistic against a noise-only null built from the split-half data you already collect: report neighborhood A-vs-B sign disagreement as the floor, and claim P2 only if global-vs-neighborhood disagreement exceeds it; do the same for E3b and for P6's rank correlation. (2) Close the backfill hole: either freeze the retrieved bundle composition when evaluating the screened bank (evaluate B(q) minus removed items, at reduced k, so the estimand matches the estimator) or add a third split-half term that measures the utility of promoted items in their new bundles, and stop calling the residual 'interference' until backfill is subtracted. Reporting bank-size and bundle-overlap statistics between screened and unscreened deployment is the minimum. (3) Report the EB posterior distribution before committing: with m~12 and tiny per-item effects, tau^2 will be near zero and the P(u_i>0)>0.7 rule degenerates to keep-almost-all (if mu>0) or keep-almost-none (if mu<0, which the pilot's harmful bank predicts). In the second case the EB cell is mechanically a no-memory cell and the headline contrast is vacuous; the risk-factor pre-check catches an empty bank but not this degeneracy. (4) Re-probe under instruction B for at least a subset so E5 becomes an interaction contrast (screen-fit-on-A vs screen-fit-on-B, both evaluated under B) instead of a replication that cannot distinguish co-adaptation from B simply being harder. (5) Execute a real literature search before submission.
reviews.missing_baseline: An oracle / held-out-fit screen: fit the admission rule directly on the evaluation labels and report it as a ceiling cell. Without it, the very likely outcome (screened bank indistinguishable from no-memory) is uninterpretable - a reviewer cannot tell whether the bank simply contains no positive-utility items, whether item-level admission is the wrong granularity, or whether the probe budget is too small, and the proposal's headline negative result becomes unattributable. Two smaller omissions a reviewer would also name: EB-screened at k=3 (you compare EB@k=7 against unscreened@k=3, so screening and volume are never crossed at the same injection budget, and the random size/token-matched control does not substitute for that cell); and a bundle-level selector - greedy or submodular forward selection over bundles at the same 3,200-episode probe budget - which is the obvious competitor once interference is named as a candidate mechanism, and which the proposal relegates to a framing sentence ('screen bundles, not items') in P4's refutation clause. The bandit curator (baseline 8) does not fill this gap: Thompson sampling over a 240-arm keep/drop space with episode-level shared credit at 3,200 episodes (~13 episodes per item) is constructed to lose, and predicting that your paired estimator beats it is not informative about the RL-curation line it is standing in for.
reviews.preprint_collision: This is the weakest section of the submission and I judge it as a negative, not a neutral. The check reports zero executed searches - two consecutive rounds of tool failure - no titles, no dates, no CLOSEST/GAP table, and an explicitly 'unverified recollection' list. By the standard that novelty must be established rather than asserted, novelty here is simply not established, and the honesty about that (which I do credit for integrity) does not substitute for the search. The proposed mitigation - pre-emptively retargeting the headline to the selection-noise decomposition so a colliding screening preprint would not subsume the paper - is sensible risk management but it moves the novelty burden onto exactly the half that is the least novel in the abstract (winner's curse plus EB shrinkage is standard machinery) and the least identified in the design (see strongest_objection). The specific collisions I would want checked before I could support acceptance: 2025-26 arXiv work on validation overfitting / selection noise in prompt and demonstration optimizers (MIPRO/GEPA-class gains shrinking on true held-out sets), which is the same selection-on-noise claim in an adjacent setting; the 2025 agentic-memory curation line (ReasoningBank, Memory-R1, A-MEM/Mem0-style consolidation) for utility-based or reward-based admission; and Shapley/LOO demonstration-valuation preprints for retrieval-conditioned example scoring. The authors' own stated collision criterion (a preprint doing both neighborhood-conditional counterfactual utility and a split-sample transfer analysis) is drawn narrowly enough that it would clear almost anything; a reviewer will apply a looser one.
